lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: My Reading Life: Recommend a Book
lesson.summary: Explore what you like to read and recommend books with a personal reason.
learning_objectives: Reflect on what you like to read
Recommend a text with two reasons
Present a text in a new form

standards.text: Read for pleasure; discuss and recommend books with reasons; read a wide range of genres, including poetry, plays and non-fiction

success_criteria: I can say what I like to read and why
I can recommend a book with two reasons
I can help curate a shelf for everyone
lesson.real_life: Urdu and English books at home, Pakistani and British children's authors, and the school library and public library in the UK.

warm_up.explanation: A genre is a type of book.

sub_lessons.title: What do I like to read?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: what makes a good recommendation?
blocks.say: Today we think about our own reading lives. We find out what we like and share it with others.

blocks.alt: A tall white shelving unit packed with many different books in neat square sections
blocks.caption: A big shelf of books. Every reader chooses different things from it.
blocks.credit: Photo by Aleksei Ieshkin on Unsplash
blocks.say: In Islam, the first word revealed in the Qur'an is Iqra, which means read. Reading matters in many cultures.

blocks.markdown: A **preference** is something you like more than other things.
blocks.say: Your reading history is the story of what you have read so far. Think about books at home in Urdu and English.

scenes.caption: First book.
scenes.say: Think back. What was the first book you loved? Maybe a picture book.

scenes.caption: Now.
scenes.say: Think of now. What do you read at home, at school or at the library?

scenes.caption: Patterns.
scenes.say: Notice patterns. Do you like funny stories, facts or poems?

question.explanation: A preference is what you like.

blocks.markdown: **Appreciating** a character means saying what is good about them.
blocks.say: Characters can help us find books we love. We might like brave, funny or clever characters.
A fair way to say it: I like this character because they never give up.

scenes.caption: Pick.
scenes.say: Pick a character you like. Say their name.

scenes.caption: An action.
scenes.say: Say one thing they do. For example, they help a friend.

scenes.caption: Your reason.
scenes.say: Say why it matters to you. That is your personal reason.

question.prompt: A reason for liking a character should say why you like them.

blocks.title: Nadia swaps a story
blocks.transcript: Nadia has a favourite story. She wants to share it. She swaps books with a classmate. Reason one: the plot has a surprising twist. Reason two: it reminds her of a trip with her grandmother. Nadia pitches the book in twenty seconds. The class puts books on a shared shelf. Her classmate tries a genre she has never read. Together, they build a reading community.
blocks.caption: Nadia swaps a favourite story with a classmate and finds two reasons to recommend it.

points: Give a reason for liking a character
blocks.say: Let us remember. Think about your reading history, favourite characters and reasons.

blocks.markdown: A **form** is the shape of a text.
blocks.say: Texts come in many forms. A form is how a text is shaped, such as a poem, a comic or a fact book.

blocks.alt: Colourful book spines in a row on a shelf, blurred at the edges
blocks.caption: A row of book spines. Each book on a shelf can have a different form and genre.
blocks.credit: Photo by Pierre Bamin on Unsplash
blocks.say: All forms count as real reading. A comic makes us read pictures and words together.

scenes.caption: A poem.
scenes.say: A poem is short, with careful words. Poems can rhyme or not.

scenes.caption: A comic.
scenes.say: A comic tells a story in pictures and speech bubbles.

scenes.caption: Facts.
scenes.say: A non-fiction book gives facts. You can dip in and out of it.

question.prompt: Which is a form of text?

blocks.markdown: Trying new things helps us learn what we like.
blocks.say: Try a form you do not usually read. You might find a new favourite.

blocks.title: Fiction or fact?
blocks.goal: Move each book. A made-up story goes in Fiction. A book of facts goes in Non-fiction.
blocks.say: Now sort the books by what they are. Is each one fiction or non-fiction?

blocks.title: Try a new form
materials: A poem, a comic or a fact book
instructions: Pick a form you have not read much.
Write one thing you liked and one question.
Tell a partner what you tried.

question.prompt: A comic counts as real reading.
question.hint: Think about reading words and pictures.

points: A form is the shape of a text

blocks.say: Let us remember. Texts come in many forms and every form counts.

blocks.markdown: A **pitch** is a short talk to persuade.
blocks.say: In book speed-dating, you pitch a book in twenty seconds. A pitch is a short, exciting spoken advert.

scenes.caption: Name.
scenes.say: First, name the book and its author.

scenes.caption: A reason.
scenes.say: Next, give one reason that is personal. I loved it because it made me laugh.

scenes.caption: Who.
scenes.say: Finally, say who might enjoy it. Keep it short and clear.

question.prompt: Pick two things a good pitch includes.
question.explanation: Name and reason fit a short pitch.

blocks.markdown: A **genre** is a type of book.
blocks.say: A genre is a type of story, like adventure, mystery or fantasy. Listen for clues and guess.

blocks.title: Genre game
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Warm up your memory. Watch the genre pictures light up, then copy them.

question.prompt: A story with a dragon and a wizard is which genre?

points: A pitch is short and clear
A genre is a type of book
blocks.say: Let us remember. Pitch a book briefly with a personal reason, and listen for the genre.

terms.meaning: A short talk to persuade.

blocks.say: A recommendation says why someone should read a book. It gives two reasons, one personal and one about the book.

scenes.caption: Title.
scenes.say: Start with the title and author.

scenes.caption: Two reasons.
scenes.say: Give two reasons. One is about the story and one is about you.

scenes.caption: Who.
scenes.say: End by saying who might enjoy it.

question.prompt: How many reasons should a recommendation give?

blocks.markdown: **Curate** means to choose and arrange with care.
blocks.say: To curate means to choose and arrange things carefully. A curated shelf has many kinds of books.

blocks.markdown: A good shelf has something for everyone.
blocks.say: A class or home shelf can hold books in Urdu and English, poems, comics and facts. A school or public library in the UK works the same way.

scenes.caption: A mix.
scenes.say: Choose books in many forms and genres. Include some that are not your own favourites.

scenes.caption: A card.
scenes.say: Add a card to each book with a recommendation.

scenes.caption: A rota.
scenes.say: Make a rota so everyone has a turn to look after the shelf.
